definition: In this context, a sex object is a dehumanized view of a person that centers on physical appearance and sexualized evaluation rather than the person as a whole. The term is used in discussing how activating this kind of mental schema can contribute to self-objectification.

reasons: The packet mentions activation of the “sex object” schema as one proposed mechanism, but it does not define that term as a dehumanized, appearance- and sexuality-centered view of a person.

The packet does not support the claim that this schema is used to explain self-objectification in the detailed way stated; it only says the schema is one mechanism among four that may trigger reported effects.

The packet supports that objectification involves concerns about one’s physical appearance and treating oneself as a dehumanized object, but it does not specifically support the definition’s claim that the process “centers on … sexualized evaluation rather than the person as a whole.”

The definition’s wording goes beyond what the packet explicitly provides about what the “sex object” schema consists of (the packet mentions activation of a “sex object” schema, and separately discusses components like appearance concerns and dehumanized treatment, but not the specific emphasis on “sexualized evaluation”).
